# QS-CFW-7855-84 Quality specification - valve body CFW-7855-84 (F316)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-7855-84

Scope
This quality specification establishes acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for the valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) forged in F316 material at Plant P1. It applies to all incoming forgings, in-process forgings, and final machined valve bodies delivered to internal assembly or customer shipment. Background and rationale: valve body sealing and mechanical performance are driven by material hardness, internal bore geometry, and control of forging mass. The requirements herein are chosen to balance machinability, toughness, and dimensional stability for this geometry and alloy.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for the part. Values are batch-level pass/fail limits to be used by production and quality control.

- Characteristic: Hardness (post-forge, prior to final machining)  
  Requirement: The hardness range for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 32-36 HRC.

- Characteristic: Bore diameter tolerancing (as-forged or after rough bore operation where specified on the print)  
  Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is ±0.05 mm.

- Characteristic: Forging mass (as cast/forged blank condition, prior to finish machining)  
  Requirement: The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 105.0 kg.

Notes on table application
- Hardness is specified on the as-forged or heat-treated condition referenced on manufacturing travelers. The range is intended to prevent excessive hardness that would impede machining and to retain sufficient strength for service. Hardness outside the range is treated as nonconforming unless dispositioned per the nonconformance handling section.
- Bore diameter tolerance applies to specified bores identified on the engineering drawing for this part. For assemblies requiring interference or clearance fits, the drawing overrides this table and must be consulted first. The tolerance is a final-inspection acceptance band; process controls should target a centered nominal value to reduce scrap.
- Maximum forging weight is used to screen incoming blanks and to control forging die life and handling capacity. Shipments of blanks heavier than the stated maximum must be rejected or returned unless an approved deviation is issued.

Inspection method
General principles
Inspections shall be performed by trained quality personnel using calibrated equipment traceable to the plant calibration program. Records listed below must be retained in the document control system and linked to each lot or serial number.

Hardness inspection
- Location: Hardness shall be measured at the locations defined on the inspection drawing or on representative surfaces that are not affected by machining or scale removal. Where multiple readings are required per part, follow the sampling pattern on the inspection traveler.
- Equipment: Use Rockwell hardness testers configured for the Rockwell C scale. Ensure indenter and load are appropriate for HRC measurements and that the unit is within current calibration.
- Acceptance: Report each reading and the lot average. Compare results against the requirement: The hardness range for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 32-36 HRC. Parts or lots with readings outside this range require disposition.

Bore diameter inspection
- Location: Measure the bore at the intended functional surfaces and at locations specified on the drawing. Take measurements after any rough-boring operation and again after final machining as required by the process step.
- Equipment: Use calibrated bore gauges or internal micrometers suitable for the bore geometry. Surface finish and geometry may require specialized gauges; use non-deforming contact methods for soft or unfinished surfaces.
- Acceptance: Each measured bore must meet the tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is ±0.05 mm. Record individual measurements, the nominal target dimension from the drawing, and whether the measurement lies within the allowable band.

Forging weight inspection
- Location: Weigh the forging blank after derusting and prior to major machining operations that remove significant mass.
- Equipment: Use calibrated scales or load cells consistent with plant calibration practice.
- Acceptance: Verify that the blank does not exceed the stated limit: The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 105.0 kg. If a blank exceeds this mass, segregate and notify quality and production engineering for investigation.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A lot of blanks shows a hardness average near the lower bound but with occasional readings below the range. These parts should be quarantined and a root cause analysis conducted to determine whether heat treatment or cooling variations caused the deviation. Rework by approved heat treatment may be considered if metallurgical evaluation supports it.
- Example: A bore measured at final inspection is outside the ±0.05 mm band on one axis due to ovality. The part should be evaluated for machining correction if the drawing allows material removal; otherwise, designate as scrap or reworkable per disposition.

Records to keep
- Hardness test reports with individual readings and equipment calibration identifier.  
- Bore measurement records including gauge identifier, nominal dimension, and measured values.  
- Weight records for each blank with scale identifier.  
- Nonconformance reports and dispositions when a requirement is not met.  
- Traveler or process sheet linking inspection records to the batch or serial number.

Nonconformance handling
Initial screening and quarantine
- Any part or lot failing to meet the hardness, bore tolerance, or forging weight requirements must be clearly marked and segregated from conforming material. Do not proceed to assembly or shipment.

Investigation and disposition
- Quality shall initiate an investigation to determine the root cause of the nonconformance. Actions may include review of heat-treatment records, operator logs, tooling condition, and incoming raw material certificates. Where corrective heat treatment, machining, or other rework is feasible and documented, a formal disposition must be issued before returning parts to production.
- Dispositions must be documented and retained with the inspection records. Records must state the corrective action taken and the verification method to confirm acceptance after rework.

Customer notification and reporting
- If nonconformance affects material previously shipped or is a systematic process failure, notify the customer per plant communication procedures and retain copies of the notification and corrective action report.

Final note
Adherence to this specification ensures consistent part performance and reduces downstream rework. All personnel performing inspections or dispositions on valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) must be familiar with this document and the associated inspection travelers and drawings.
